summary: iter91 — End-to-end backend verification of (A) 'Everyone' delivery zone and (B) Recharge-operator ↔ shop sub-category sync. Built new pytest suite backend/tests/test_iter91_everyone_and_recharge_e2e.py with 22 tests across 5 phases (zone E2E, customer visibility, checkout COD/online/wallet rules, normal-vendor regression, recharge sync + delete-guard). All 22 PASS against the live FastAPI backend. Mocked Razorpay (pay_MOCK_*) exercised for the online-far checkout path. Vendor's original delivery config and all seeded data (products, recharge options, edit requests, cart) cleaned up on teardown.

minor.issue: ProductCreate pydantic model only exposes `sub_category` (underscore), not `subcategory`. Clients sending the un-underscored name silently drop the field. The recharge filter already queries both shapes, so this is cosmetic — but the admin product form / vendor form must send `sub_category`.
`limit` is capped at 300 (pydantic le=300). Documenting here so future test harnesses don't ask for 500 and get a 422.

action_items: No action required — both features are production-ready at the backend. (A) 'Everyone' zone correctly flips products visible at any pincode, blocks COD / wallet_cod on far shipments, and still permits COD at the vendor's own pincode. (B) Recharge operator add → vendor product under operator → unpublished hidden → admin publish → listed → delete blocked while products exist (409) → delete allowed when empty — all mirrored into shop_categories.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/products_public.py:_eligible_cache has a 60s TTL and is busted only by admin endpoints that call `bust_products_public_caches()`. Any code path that mutates a vendor's `delivery_radius_mode` / `delivery_pincodes` / `delivery_radius_km` via direct DB write (migrations, seeds, reset-centre scripts, admin UI shortcuts) must call that helper too, else the customer shop and the checkout guard will keep serving stale eligibility for up to a minute. Confirmed by failing-then-fixing regression test_32 in this run.

models.py:ProductCreate exposes only `sub_category` (underscore). The vendor Add-Product screen posts via this model; recharge sub-category selections rendered as `subcategory` would be silently dropped. The listing path (routes/recharge.py) already OR's both field names, so the sync is forgiving, but the model should probably accept an alias to avoid vendor confusion.
updated_files: testvendor@test.com password hash in users collection — rotated to a fresh bcrypt of Test@1234 because the stored hash no longer validated. All 4 preview accounts (admin, testvendor, testvendor2 untouched, testbuyer) now authenticate with the credentials in /app/memory/test_credentials.md.
seed_data_creation: All seeded data created inside the test (ITER91Op recharge option, ITER91 Plan vendor product, ITER91 Everywhere Widget direct seed, two vendor_edit_requests) is deleted in the module-scoped teardown. Vendor's `delivery_radius_mode` / `delivery_radius_km` / `delivery_pincodes` / `store_pincode` / `pincode` are snapshotted and restored to the pre-test values (`both` / 10km / ['517641','517645'] / 517644).
context_for_next_testing_agent: The vendor password-hash reset is persistent and does NOT need to be redone. Pytest file lives at backend/tests/test_iter91_everyone_and_recharge_e2e.py — reruns are idempotent (teardown restores vendor + wipes seeds). Mongo-level cache (routes/products_public._eligible_cache) is 60s; if you flip vendor delivery mode via raw DB write and the test later hits /products or /orders/checkout you WILL see stale results — use the vendor_edit_requests → admin approve flow instead so bust_products_public_caches() runs.
rca_of_issue: No bugs found in the implementation under test. Two self-inflicted test harness issues were caught and fixed before the final run: (1) `GET /products?limit=500` → 422 because the server caps `limit` at 300; (2) `test_30_revert_vendor_to_both_mode` originally wrote to Mongo directly and the 60s in-memory `_eligible_cache` still said 'this vendor delivers everywhere' when the regression checkout ran — rewriting the test to go through the real vendor-edit-request flow (which calls `bust_products_public_caches()` on approval) resolved it. Both fixes are documented inline in the pytest file.
